title: TIS-DPO: Token-level Importance Sampling for Direct Preference Optimization With Estimated Weights

contributions.purpose: Fix DPO's treatment of a whole response as a single arm, which ignores that different tokens have different rewards and hurts optimization efficiency.
contributions.mechanism: TIS-DPO: a token-level importance sampling DPO objective. Argues optimal data has equal expected token rewards; since the optimal dataset is unavailable, it uses the actual dataset for importance sampling, assigning each token an importance weight based on its reward to obtain unbiased optimization.
contributions.evaluation: Significantly outperforms baseline methods (standard DPO and others) on harmlessness and helpfulness alignment and on summarization tasks (qualitative; per-dataset numbers in tables).
contributions.source_quote: We propose TIS-DPO, a novel token-level importance sampling approach that improves DPO by considering token-level rewards.

contributions.purpose: Estimate the unknown token-level importance weights needed by the TIS-DPO objective.
contributions.mechanism: Three practical methods to build contrastive LLMs and estimate token weights from their prediction-probability differences: (1) contrastive prompts on the original LLM, (2) contrastive SFT training two LLMs on winning vs losing responses, (3) forward/reverse DPO training.
contributions.evaluation: Each method offers a different trade-off between implementation complexity and effectiveness; weight visualizations show the estimates identify key token positions.
contributions.source_quote: We develop three practical methods to estimate token-level weights through contrastive LLMs.

contributions.purpose: Empirically validate that token-level importance weighting improves alignment and generation quality.
contributions.mechanism: Experiments across alignment and summarization datasets, plus visualization of estimated token weights.
contributions.evaluation: Improves model safety on alignment datasets without compromising usability and enhances summary quality; outperforms standard DPO and other baselines across multiple datasets.
contributions.source_quote: Extensive experiments demonstrate significant improvements in model alignment and generation quality across multiple datasets.

self_declared_provenance.quote: In this paper, we propose TIS-DPO (Token-level Importance Sampling DPO), which does not require modifying the original data construction process. Instead, it uses real data to perform importance sampling on the optimal data ... Zeng et al. (2024) proposed token-level DPO but did not explicitly consider varying token importance. Some work has considered token weights during DPO training data collection (Xie et al., 2024; Lai et al., 2024).
Inspired by previous work (Rafailov et al., 2024a), we use the difference in token prediction probabilities between contrastive LLMs to estimate each token's reward.

notes: Accept paper. Positions itself against DPO (Rafailov 2024b), token-credit-assignment DPO (Rafailov 2024a), token-level DPO (Zeng 2024), and data-collection-based token weighting (Xie 2024; Lai 2024), emphasizing it needs no change to data construction. Notes implementation-complexity vs effectiveness trade-off across the three weight-estimation methods; no negative results highlighted.
